decks.notes: This deck focuses on using low-cost spells and efficient creatures to apply pressure on the opponent quickly. By leveraging powerful spells like Ancestral Recall and Treasure Cruise, along with disruptive cards like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares, the deck aims to maintain control of the game while steadily building card advantage. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value from the graveyard, creating a versatile and resilient strategy that can out-tempo and out-value opponents in a 1 vs 1 format.

The deck revolves around using Bazaar of Baghdad to quickly fill the graveyard with creatures like Squee, Goblin Nabob and Basking Rootwalla, enabling the early casting of powerful threats like Vengevine and Hollow One. The deck also utilizes cards like Noxious Revival and Force of Will to protect its game plan, while also including disruptive elements like Mindbreak Trap and Force of Negation. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm opponents with efficient threats and disruptive spells, maintaining pressure throughout the game.

This deck aims to aggressively put pressure on the opponent by utilizing powerful creatures like Vengevine, Hogaak, and Hollow One. By utilizing cards like Bazaar of Baghdad to fill up the graveyard, the deck can quickly recur creatures and overwhelm the opponent. The inclusion of disruptive creatures like Collector Ouphe and Deathrite Shaman also helps to disrupt the opponent's strategies. The deck also includes a number of powerful mana acceleration cards like Moxen and Black Lotus to quickly deploy threats and maintain tempo.

This deck revolves around utilizing powerful artifacts, such as Moxen and Mana Vault, alongside draw and tutor spells to generate massive amounts of mana and card advantage. By combining cards like Paradoxical Outcome with artifacts like Bolas's Citadel and Time Vault, the deck is able to create explosive combo turns that can win the game in a single activation. Additionally, disruptive elements like Mindbreak Trap and Force of Will provide protection against opposing strategies, while cards like Teferi, Time Raveler and Narset, Parter of Veils help control the pace of the game.

The deck revolves around assembling the necessary pieces to cast Doomsday and then use the spell to set up a win condition involving Thassa's Oracle. The deck includes tutors, card draw, counterspells, and fast mana to efficiently dig for and cast Doomsday, leading to a combo finish with Thassa's Oracle. The deck is built to be able to quickly and consistently find and execute the combo, keeping the opponent off balance and unable to disrupt the plan.

The main concept of this vintage aggro deck is to utilize the Bazaar of Baghdad to quickly fill up the graveyard with cards like Squee, Goblin Nabob and Vengevine, triggering powerful abilities and creating a strong board presence. The deck also focuses on ramping up mana with cards like Gaea's Cradle and utilizing disruptive elements like Collector Ouphe and Force of Vigor to disrupt the opponent's game plan. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive creatures and powerful synergies, all while disrupting their strategy.

This deck is a control deck that focuses on manipulating the opponent's resources and disrupting their game plan. It utilizes a combination of card draw, tutor effects, and counterspells to maintain card advantage and control the board. The deck also includes powerful artifacts like Moxes and Time Vault to generate additional resources and gain a tempo advantage. The strong presence of counterspells, along with removal spells like Swords to Plowshares, allow the deck to deal with threats efficiently. The deck aims to slow down the opponent's game plan and outvalue them in the long run.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck focuses on utilizing Underworld Breach to enable powerful combo plays. The deck includes a variety of powerful spells like Tinker, Time Walk, and Ancestral Recall, as well as key artifacts like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel. With a mix of tutors, countermagic, and card draw, the goal is to quickly assemble the combo pieces needed to win the game. Additionally, cards like Narset, Parter of Veils and Opposition Agent provide disruption against opponents, while Urza's Saga offers additional utility and card advantage.

The deck focuses on putting pressure on the opponent with aggressive creatures while also disrupting their game plan with hatebears like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria. The goal is to slow down the opponent's spells and mana development while using efficient creatures to close out the game quickly. The deck also includes powerful one-off cards like Solitude and Emeria's Call to provide additional versatility and resilience. Overall, the strategy revolves around applying pressure and disruption to control the pace of the game and come out on top.

Using a combination of powerful draw spells, disruption, and the Doomsday combo, this deck aims to quickly assemble the cards needed to win the game by casting Doomsday and then utilizing Thassa's Oracle to win on the spot. The deck also includes a control element with cards like Force of Will and Flusterstorm to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan. With efficient mana acceleration and tutoring ability, this deck seeks to win the game in a fast and consistent manner.

The deck focuses on using fast mana cards and rituals to quickly combo off and win the game without needing any lands on the battlefield. By using cards like Balustrade Spy and Undercity Informer to mill the deck, players can then win instantly with Thassa's Oracle or Goblin Charbelcher. The deck includes protection spells like Pact of Negation and Force of Will to ensure the combo resolves successfully. The key to winning with this deck is efficient use of resources and timing the combo correctly to secure victory.

This deck focuses on assembling the Doomsday combo quickly and efficiently to win the game. It uses various cantrips, tutors, and counterspells to find and protect the Doomsday card, which is used to set up a winning pile with Thassa's Oracle. The deck aims to be fast and resilient, with the ability to disrupt opponents while quickly assembling its own win condition. The key strategy is to carefully plan out the Doomsday pile and execute it successfully to secure victory before the opponent can respond effectively.

This deck revolves around utilizing the powerful combo with Underworld Breach to generate infinite mana and draw the entire deck, eventually culminating in a Brain Freeze win condition. The deck includes various tutors, fast mana sources, and counterspells to protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's strategy. The inclusion of Time Vault and key artifacts like Sol Ring and Mana Crypt accelerates the combo potential, while cards like Tolarian Academy and Merchant Scroll provide additional utility. Overall, the deck is focused on efficiently assembling the combo and quickly executing a game-winning sequence.

The deck focuses on controlling the opponent's actions and resources through counterspells, removal spells, and disruptive creatures like Lavinia and Narset. It also aims to search for key combo pieces like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel to gain an advantage. The deck has a strong mana base with powerful acceleration from cards like Sol Ring and the Moxen, allowing for quick and efficient plays. The primary win condition is to assemble the Time Vault combo or generate value through cards like Monastery Mentor and Sphinx of the Steel Wind.

The deck focuses on aggressive creatures that also disrupt the opponent's strategy with hate cards. By combining hatebears with powerful mana acceleration, the deck aims to lock down the opponent's options while quickly deploying threats. Cards like Spirit of the Labyrinth, Thalia, Guardian of Thraben, and Archon of Emeria slow down the opponent, while Urza's Saga and other mana acceleration cards allow the deck to quickly build a board presence. The deck's strategy is to overwhelm the opponent with efficient creatures and disrupt their game plan at the same time.

This deck focuses on assembling a powerful combo using Coveted Jewel as a key piece. By generating a large amount of mana with cards like Grim Monolith and Mishra's Workshop, the deck can cast Coveted Jewel and activate its ability multiple times in a single turn. This allows the player to draw a large number of cards, generate more mana, and eventually win the game through card advantage and overwhelming the opponent. Cards like Tinker and Paradoxical Outcome help to find and recur Coveted Jewel, while disruptive spells like Force of Will and Pact of Negation protect the combo.
